title: Leaking Kernel Pointers Through a USB Stick — KASLR Bypass via sierra_ms.c
excerpt: A missing length check in the Sierra Wireless USB storage driver let a malicious device serve a short control transfer and leave stale kmalloc-64 heap bytes in a world-readable sysfs attribute. This post walks through the bug, turns it into a full KASLR bypass with slab grooming, and shows the before/after of the fix that is now merged into every maintained stable kernel tree.

title: Capability Hardware Enhanced RISC Instructions — Part 1
excerpt: CHERI replaces forgeable integer pointers with unforgeable hardware capabilities that carry bounds, permissions, and a validity tag. This primer covers the memory-safety threat model, the capability model's three invariants, and how tagged memory works.
